hm_sub: What this tool does, and where you are in the workflow.
hm_what: MalDroid Insight is a workbench for building and evaluating machine-learning models that tell malware from benign apps. Bring any malware dataset as a CSV file, train several models with a leakage-free pipeline, compare them, see which features drive their decisions, and classify new samples.
hm_pipe: Every model goes through the same steps, in this order, so no information from the test data leaks into training: log1p → RobustScaler → SMOTE (training data only) → model.
hm_s1_d: Upload a CSV or add an example. Choose the label column and which values mean Benign.
hm_s2_d: Look at class balance, missing values and the features that best separate the classes.
hm_s3_d: Choose features and models, then train with a hold-out split and cross-validation.
hm_s4_d: See accuracy, F1, confusion matrices and the differences between runs.
hm_s5_d: Find out which features drive a model's decisions (SHAP).
hm_s6_d: Classify new samples with a trained model.
hm_cross: Optional: Cross-Dataset tests whether a model trained on one dataset still works on another.
hm_none: No dataset yet. Add one to get started.
gl_log1p_d: A transform, log(1 + x), that compresses very large counts so a few huge values do not dominate.
gl_scaler_d: Rescales each feature using the median and interquartile range, so outliers have little influence.
gl_smote_d: Creates synthetic samples of the minority class to balance the training data. Applied to the training split only.
gl_leak_d: The model sees information it would not have in real use (for example a column derived from the label), so results look better than they are.
gl_holdout_d: One fixed split (here 80% train, 20% test) used to measure performance on unseen data.
gl_cv_d: Repeats training and testing on several different splits (folds). The spread between folds shows how stable the result is.
gl_shap_d: Measures how much each feature pushed a prediction toward or away from a class.
ds_sub: Add datasets, check their quality and explore their features. Any CSV malware dataset works.
ds_dist_help: A strong imbalance between classes can make accuracy misleading; the pipeline balances the training data with SMOTE.
ds_sep_help: A higher score means the feature differs more between Benign and malware samples. Very high scores on metadata columns can signal label leakage.
ds_delete_confirm: Yes, delete {name} and all runs that use it
ad_example_note: The example CSV files must be in the data/ folder of the project.
ad_upload_hint: CSV file. Each row is one app sample; the columns are numeric features plus one label column.
ad_benign_help: Every other value is treated as a malware class.
ad_exclude_help: IDs, hashes, or columns that may leak the label. All other numeric columns are used as features.
ad_err_name: A dataset with this name already exists.
ad_err_label: The label column needs at least two different values.
ad_err_label_many: The label column has too many different values (more than {n}); it does not look like a class label.
ad_err_benign: Select at least one Benign value and leave at least one malware value.
ad_err_feats: No usable numeric feature columns remain.
ad_warn_small: Some classes have fewer than {n} samples; SMOTE and cross-validation may fail.
